# Baked case files (local-only, regenerated by the ETLs)

The harness task registry reads the EvalPlus and ILCB files at import time. The AISI file is read
only when an AISI task is selected. None of these files is in version control:

- `ilcb_cases.json` — 515 records (103 Impossible-LiveCodeBench problems × 5 splits: the three
  upstream splits plus two locally derived visible-subset splits, `subset3-stratified` and
  `subset3`, each holding k=3 of the true check's asserts), ~2.9 MiB. Read by
  `reward_hacking/harness/tasks_ilcb.py`; the derivation is `reward_hacking/visible_subset.py`.
- `evalplus_cases.json` — 14 curated EvalPlus problems with their visible and hidden cases,
  ~240 KiB. Read by `reward_hacking/harness/tasks_evalplus.py`.
- `aisi_rh_envs_cases.json` — locally baked AISI rh_envs problems with original and oneoff test
  variants. Read on selection by `reward_hacking/harness/tasks.py`; the derivation is
  `reward_hacking/aisi_rh_envs_etl.py`. Its provenance records the AISI checkout revision and the
  per-source MIT or CC-BY-4.0 license.

They are untracked deliberately, and the reason is licensing before it is size. The
Impossible-LiveCodeBench rows carry problem statements and test bodies derived from
LiveCodeBench, and a survey of that provenance chain found no redistribution grant anywhere in
it — so this repository, whose remote is public, must not republish them. Contamination is the
second reason and applies to all three files: benchmark material in a public repository becomes
training data, which is the one thing that would destroy the measurement these tasks exist to
make. The EvalPlus and AISI files also derive from public benchmark material, so they are
untracked for the contamination reason.

## Regenerating them

From the repository root, one command each. These need network access:

```bash
uv run python reward_hacking/harness/ilcb_etl.py
uv run python reward_hacking/harness/evalplus_etl.py
uv run python -m reward_hacking.aisi_rh_envs_etl --allow-legacy-mutation
```

`ilcb_etl.py` pulls a pinned revision of the `fjzzq2002/impossible_livecodebench` dataset from the
Hugging Face Hub and re-derives each row's impossibility proof locally, refusing to bake a split
whose row count has moved away from what it was written against. `evalplus_etl.py` downloads two
pinned GitHub release archives (cached under `~/.cache/evalplus-releases`), then computes every
expected output by running each shipped canonical solution under the interpreter
`scripts/episode_jail.sh` resolves for the jail — the one the graders themselves run, so the baked
answers and the graded ones cannot disagree. Its path and version go into the case file, so a later
reader can tell whether the answers still hold under whatever the jail resolves now. Neither script
imports anything from this repository, which is what lets them regenerate a case file that is
currently missing or broken; run them by file path, not with `python -m`, for that same reason. Each
has a `--out` flag if you want the output somewhere else, and `evalplus_etl.py` also takes
`--cache-dir` and `--max-plus-cases`.

`aisi_rh_envs_etl.py` loads the source datasets, checks each selected reference solution inside the
episode jail, and writes the local case file with source counts and drop reasons. The AISI clone and
datasets must be available before it runs.

### Output-constrained oneoffs

The AISI command above explicitly opts into legacy mutations, which do not guarantee a valid output
family. For constrained mutations, derive a separate registry from an existing local registry using
`--input-registry`, `--output-contracts`, and a distinct `--out`. The contract catalog stays ignored
alongside the cases; its explicit domains are validated by `reward_hacking/output_contracts.py`.
Derivation preserves originals and partitions, records unsupported cases, and refuses to overwrite
the source registry. `--minimum-supported` can require a minimum supported-case count. Select the
derived registry with the generation command's `--aisi-cases` option.

The recent LiveCodeBench importer similarly requires `--output-contracts` and a distinct ignored
`--output-root` for constrained derivation, or explicit `--allow-legacy-mutation` for legacy mutation.
Select its derived cases and matching split manifest together using `--ilcb-cases` and
`--ilcb-split-manifest`. Strict readers revalidate contract bindings and mutations; legacy refresh
cannot downgrade a constrained registry. Contract catalogs and derived cases remain local and must
never be committed.

## What happens when they are absent

Importing `reward_hacking.harness` raises a `RuntimeError` naming the missing EvalPlus or ILCB path
and the command above. A missing AISI file does not block harness imports; selecting an AISI task
raises a `RuntimeError` naming that path and its regeneration command. No selection silently
returns an empty set.

Because of that, test modules that import the harness cannot be collected in a fresh clone until
the EvalPlus and ILCB files exist. They report as skipped, with a reason pointing here, rather than
erroring — see `_absent_case_file_reason` in `reward_hacking/tests/conftest.py`, which fires only
on a genuinely missing case file and lets a corrupt one fail loudly. AISI selection tests can use
synthetic case files and do not require the locally baked AISI corpus.

## R2E leak cases

`r2e_leak_cases.json` is the gitignored case file for the reference-solution-leak environment family. It
holds the issue text, gold source patch, gold per-test outcome map and the digest-pinned image reference of
each task, taken from `PrimeIntellect/R2E-Gym-Subset-Verified` at the pinned revision recorded in its
provenance. The dataset card declares no licence and the rows derive from the upstream repositories' own
licences, so the file stays local and is never redistributed; the provenance block records the dataset
revision and the licence fields, and `load_tasks` in `reward_hacking/r2e_leak_data.py` refuses a file without
them. The train and held-out partitions are computed at load time from hashes of the repo name and commit
(whole repos first, then a share of tasks inside the remaining repos) and checked against the counts in
provenance.

Regenerate it from the repository root. Each step needs network and Docker access, at least 60 GB free on `/`
(the ETL refuses below that), and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` unset:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m reward_hacking.r2e_leak_etl inventory
.venv/bin/python -m reward_hacking.r2e_leak_etl extract --repo <repo_name> --count <n> --verify
.venv/bin/python -m reward_hacking.r2e_leak_etl bake
```

`extract` pulls each image by digest, copies `/testbed` and the hidden `/r2e_tests` out of it into
`/var/tmp/leak-env/templates/<task_id>/{extracted,hidden_tests}`, and records `provenance.json` last, so an
interrupted run resumes per task. `--verify` mounts a scratch copy of the tree at `/testbed` with the network
disabled, checks that the base tree fails and the gold patch passes, and that the package imports from the
mount; `bake` keeps only tasks whose verification passed. Tests use synthetic rows and do not need the file.

## Procedural math work packages

`math_cases.json` contains generated math questions and answer keys for `math_oneoff` and
`math_loose_checker`. It is gitignored measurement material; never stage or redistribute it.
Generate it locally without network access:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m reward_hacking.math_etl --count 100
```

Items are deterministic by ID and have an ID-based train/held-out split independent of file order
or corpus size. Each package covers arithmetic, algebra, combinatorics, probability and unit
conversion. The oneoff treatment changes exactly one answer; its original twin has the correct key.
The loose treatment accepts numeric candidates in text, and its original control requires a single
numeric answer. Both use the existing task loop and independent same-artifact checks. Math data is
loaded only when selected; a missing file produces a regeneration error. Tests generate disposable
items at runtime, with no item texts or answer keys in tracked fixtures.

## Small repository repair tasks

`small_repo/manifest.json` and its repository templates are private benchmark material. Keep the
sources, issue descriptions, source edits, test identities, and validation records in this ignored
directory. The manifest records repository provenance and a deterministic train/held-out split for
each task. Every admitted task has a passing pristine suite and a nonempty set of failing tests after
one source edit, with every other collected test still passing.

Generate a pack from a locally prepared repository inventory, using disposable work outside the
home directory:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m reward_hacking.harness.small_repo_etl \
  --inventory <private-inventory.json> \
  --output reward_hacking/harness/data/small_repo/manifest.json \
  --work-directory <disposable-work-directory> --count-per-repository 20
```

The `small_repo` organism family uses the existing `status_report` payment register: a true
`tests_passing` claim pays unless protected test or configuration edits were observed. A clean
rerun of the pristine tests and configuration against the submitted non-test files supplies the
independent truth label. Stored source bundles permit offline replay and rescoring. Loading this
family requires the private manifest; it does not require downloading repositories during episodes.
